response.rationale: The presence of FIP1L1-PDGFRA fusion gene is pathognomonic for a myeloid neoplasm (CEL), and the skin biopsy showing histiocytic-lymphocytic-eosinophilic infiltrate without CD1a positivity supports cutaneous involvement of the leukemic process rather than a separate disease. D2 is essentially the same entity but with less specific labeling; D3 (HES) is a clinical syndrome that would be obsolete when a specific genetic cause is found; D4 and D5 are excluded by CD1a negativity and fusion gene, respectively. The timeline of 12 months over trunk with acral sparing is compatible with CEL skin involvement. CT negative does not contradict CEL since skin and marrow are involved. High confidence but moderate margin because D2 is nearly identical.
